name: Fetch MCP Server
what: One of the official MCP reference servers. It gives the agent a single fetch tool that downloads a web page and converts the HTML to markdown, and it can read long pages in chunks. By default it refuses private, loopback and other non-public addresses (checking every redirect) and follows robots.txt for requests the model makes. Version 2026.10.24 (25 Oct 2026) includes security fixes to those checks.
who: Anyone who wants their agent to read a docs page, changelog or article by URL without a full browser.

setup.text: Install uv (recommended); uvx then runs the server with no separate install. This is the one reference server that isn't a Node package: it's a Python package on PyPI (Python 3.10 or newer), so the Node 24 requirement of the other reference servers doesn't apply.
Add to your MCP client config:
Or install with pip and run it as a module:

Already using it? Releases from 2026.10.19 need the MCP Python SDK 2.x (mcp>=2.3,<3), and 2026.10.24 is the security-fix release, so make sure you're on at least that. Calling a tool the server doesn't have now returns a JSON-RPC -32602 error instead of a tool-error result.

On Windows, if the server times out, the README suggests setting PYTHONIOENCODING to utf-8 in the server's env block. The README also documents optional --ignore-robots-txt, --user-agent and --proxy-url arguments. The --allow-private-ips argument turns off the private-address guard, so only use it for a local or internal site you trust.
Optional: install Node.js too; the server then uses a more robust HTML simplifier.

install.name: fetch
notes: This one is a Python package, so it needs uv installed rather than Node.js.

prompts: Fetch https://nextjs.org/docs and summarize what's new on that page.
Read this changelog URL and list the breaking changes.
